question: Observation
answer:
I took this photo during my maths lecture at UCSB. The classroom was quiet except for the sound of the professor writing on the chalkboard and students turning pages or typing on their laptops. Most students were busy taking notes while the professor carefully explained comparison theorems for improper integrals. Some students leaned forward in their seats while others quietly followed the examples on their computers or notebooks. Even though everyone was working on their own, the room still felt connected because students were sharing the same attention and effort.

What I noticed was how patient everyone was in the classroom. The professor wrote step-by-step instructions on the board, while the students tried to understand the difficult material together. Everyone was quiet, but it felt like we were all working together. The atmosphere felt serious but supportive at the same time.
The professor’s detailed explanations show a form of mentorship and care through patience and guidance.
The students’ focus and participation reflect shared effort and trust within the classroom environment.
